name: S.P. Apparels Ltd
title: S.P. Apparels Ltd - 540048 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: S.P. Apparels Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% YoY to INR 452.2 crores; H1 PAT up 11.9% to INR 61.9 crores on better mix.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 452.2 crores grew 12.8% QoQ and 5.8% YoY after a U.S.-tariff-hit Q1 that saw customer deferrals. Consolidated EBITDA for Q2 was INR 66.7 crores (14.7% margin, up 4.7% YoY), and PAT was INR 37.1 crores, up 6.8% YoY. Young Brand Apparels (YBAPL) and SPUK drove growth, while the parent's Avinashi base business and Sri Lanka ramp-up lagged. Management reiterated FY27 guidance but signalled about 95% achievement on revenue, with Sri Lanka tracking INR 150-170 crores against an earlier INR 190 crores plan.

segments.name: Garment division incl. Young Brand Apparels (YBAPL)
segments.commentary: H1 adjusted EBITDA INR 123.6 crores, margin 16.8% vs 15.9% in H1 FY26. Management attributed the YoY margin dip in Q2 to Sri Lanka revenue (~INR 60 crores, ~10% margin, no 6.5% duty drawback) and pre-operative costs.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparels
segments.commentary: Q2 adjusted revenue INR 109.1 crores, up 29.4% YoY on 7.6 million pieces; H1 adjusted EBITDA INR 30.7 crores (+34.7%), PAT INR 19.1 crores (+29%). Order book INR 175 crores; capacity about 1,100 machines running, targeted 1,250-1,300 by year-end.

segments.name: S.P. Apparels Avinashi (standalone)
segments.commentary: H1 adjusted EBITDA margin 16.7% (vs 16.5%) and PAT INR 51.5 crores (+9.1%). Q2 standalone revenue about INR 290 crores vs about INR 308 crores a year earlier, attributed to yarn-related (about 20%) impact and U.S. deferrals; order book INR 450 crores.

segments.name: SPUK (UK business)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 38.1 crores, up 111.8% YoY from INR 18 crores; H1 revenue INR 71 crores vs INR 33 crores. Order book GBP 4.5 million; guided EBITDA breakeven in Q3 and positive in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Sri Lanka operations
segments.commentary: H1 revenue about INR 45 crores per CFO, with 70 crores quoted by the CEO for H1 (inconsistent in transcript); H2 expected INR 80 crores, FY27 INR 150 crores. Four factories, 1,700 machines; one factory awaiting customer approval.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EBITDA close to INR 15 crores.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 EBITDA INR 0.5 crores vs loss of INR 1.5 crores in H1 FY26; EBITDA positive for 5 consecutive quarters. 45 exclusive stores; online/D2C grew threefold. Angel and Rocket: 7 stores, about INR 70 lakhs monthly store revenue, online about 50% of turnover, about 12-15% of Retail mix.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue: management says on track for INR 2,000 crores guidance but CFO expects about 95% achievement.
Garment division EBITDA margin guided at about 15% on a consolidated basis (SPAL plus Sri Lanka).
FY28 guidance: 10-15% growth for the group; Sri Lanka revenue target about INR 400 crores (earlier plan), now seen as near INR 400 crores once fourth factory approved.
Young Brand Apparels growth at least 20% in FY28, driven by Salem expansion.
SPUK target INR 500 crores revenue in 3-5 years, with 50-100% growth over next 2-3 years per management.

Retail: target PBT profitability for 3 more quarters, cash profitability within about 6 months; plan to convert parent debt to equity this financial year and later raise external capital (PE or SME listing).
capex_capacity: Standalone machines 5,700 across group at 74% utilisation in Q2 (vs 4,950 machines a year earlier); utilisation target about 80% near term and 80-85% by end-March 2027.

Sri Lanka: four factories, 1,700 machines; fourth factory (about 500 machines, second largest) awaiting customer approval, expected by end-March with shipments from April 2027; plan for 1-2 more factories (about 1,000 machines) in FY28.
Avinashi: adding about 700 machines from April 2027 by reclaiming capacity lost in FY26 due to U.S. tariffs (about 1,000 machines).

Salem (YBAPL): 40 machines running since August; 80 by mid-January, 200 then 300 machines within about 6 months; YBAPL total 1,500 machines by March per one answer, later clarified as 1,300 at year-end.
demand_pricing: Management says U.S. customers confirmed orders after tariff uncertainty eased; Q1 deferrals shifted some business into Q2.

China Plus One and diversification away from Bangladesh are driving inquiries for India and Sri Lanka; management says India landed cost is now at par with Bangladesh for fashion products post UK FTA, but Bangladesh still stronger in basic, high-volume lines.
Customer base is more than 16 customers across SPAL, SPUK and Young Brand; new UK customer shipping, new U.S. customer expected from February 2027.
Export realisation INR 162.9 per piece (+14.5% YoY) on better product mix; shift toward adult wear and older children's products.
Hedging: 80% of forex exposure hedged once orders confirmed; cotton held 30-90 days of inventory, not hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Avinashi standalone revenue decline YoY (about INR 308 crores to about INR 290 crores in Q2)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a yarn-related impact of about 20% and U.S. deferrals in Q1-Q2, expecting pickup from Q3 as U.S. customers returned.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Sri Lanka revenue below plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri Lanka FY27 now seen at INR 150-170 crores vs INR 190 crores planned, because one factory awaits customer approval; FY28 about INR 400 crores is still targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did garment margins decline YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Sri Lanka revenue (about INR 60 crores at about 10% margin, no 6.5% duty drawback) and pre-operative costs weighed on blended margin; expected to ease in 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 INR 2,000 crores revenue guidance achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on track but CFO expects about 95% achievement given revenue pushovers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Retail plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Parent provided secured loans; some may convert to equity this year as Retail debt rose. Management targets PBT profitability for 3 quarters before external capital raise; Angel and Rocket online growing 200-300% a year, with 20-25 stores by end-2028.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost down sharply YoY despite higher borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 included a forex loss on restating dollar packing credit (rupee at about INR 96-97 at June-end); rupee at about INR 94 by September reversed part of it.

risks_watch: Sri Lanka fourth factory customer approval timing (expected by end-March 2027); Sri Lanka FY27 revenue tracking below INR 190 crores plan.
Avinashi base business revenue decline YoY and yarn-related impact; recovery needed from Q3 FY27.
Garment margin dilution from Sri Lanka ramp-up (about 10% margin, no duty drawback) against 15% guidance.
SPUK EBITDA breakeven in Q3 and positive in Q4 FY27; order book GBP 4.5 million.
Retail debt rising; parent equity conversion and external fundraise pending; cash profitability targeted within about 6 months.
Rupee volatility (about INR 92-96 per USD) and 20% unhedged exposure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and FY28, but cautious on FY27 revenue, which is now seen at about 95% of guidance with Sri Lanka and Avinashi lagging. Answers on Sri Lanka approvals and Retail funding were more hedged and sometimes deferred to other executives.
key_quotes: We remain focused on delivering our guidance for FY27 and believe the progress underway positions S.P. Apparels well for the next phase of growth.
In the half year marked by orders deferral, profit growth meaningfully outpaced revenue growth.
Retail is increasingly demonstrating the strength of a more focused operating model. It is no longer a drag on the group.
So, we may end up 95% of the guidance what we have given.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR 14.9 crores in Q1 FY27 (Q1 included forex restatement loss on packing credit)

adds.what: Avinashi: about 700 machines added from April 2027 by reclaiming capacity lost in FY26 due to U.S. tariffs
Sri Lanka fourth factory (about 500 machines) awaiting customer approval, shipments from April 2027
Young Brand Apparels Salem expansion: 40 machines running, 80 by mid-January, 200-300 more within about 6 months, targeting 1,250-1,300 machines by year-end
Sri Lanka plan for 1-2 more factories (about 1,000 machines) in FY28, under evaluation

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance cut to ~95% of INR 2,000 cr (about INR 1,900 cr); FY28 guided at 10-15% growth with Sri Lanka near INR 400 cr, backed by Avinashi ~700 machines and Sri Lanka's 500-machine factory from April 2027, though Q2 utilisation was only 74% and Sri Lanka FY27 was cut to INR 150-170 cr.

oneOffs.what: Q1 FY27 included forex restatement loss on packing credit (base effect on finance cost, not revenue); Q2 finance cost INR 6.3 crores vs INR 14.9 crores in Q1 FY27
Q1 FY27 US customer deferrals shifted business into Q2; Q2 revenue INR 452.2 crores +12.8% QoQ from Q1 INR 401 crores
Q1 FY27 was a U.S.-tariff-hit quarter with customer deferrals, so QoQ comparison is against a disrupted quarter; YoY base not stated as weak

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew only 5.8% YoY to INR 452.2 crores; growth was driven by YBAPL (+29.4% on 7.6m pieces) and SPUK (+111.8%) while Avinashi fell from about INR 308 to 290 crores, and the sequential jump partly reflects U.S. orders deferred from Q1 rather than recurring demand, while export realisation rose about 14.5% on mix and PAT growth of 6.8% was helped by lower finance cost.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Garment EBITDA margin guided at about 15% consolidated for FY27, with Q2 at 14.7% group margin and H1 at 15%; Sri Lanka's ~10% margin drag is expected to ease in 2-3 months and SPUK turns EBITDA positive in Q4.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Salem YBAPL machines ramping (40 running, 80 by mid-January, 200-300 more within ~6 months) and Avinashi adds ~700 machines from April 2027 (Q4 FY27); Sri Lanka fourth factory (~500 machines) shipments from April 2027, though its customer approval is still pending.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue +12.8% QoQ and YBAPL +29.4% YoY on 7.6 mn pieces, with order book INR 175 cr at YBAPL and INR 450 cr at Avinashi; but Avinashi revenue fell YoY and group utilisation is only 74%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 74%, well below the 80% threshold, so a new capex is not forced; management says it is evaluating 1-2 more Sri Lanka factories (~1,000 machines) in FY28, which is still conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue has already been cut to about 95% of INR 2,000 cr (~INR 1,900 cr), and Sri Lanka FY27 is now INR 150-170 cr vs INR 190 cr planned.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: CFO expects only ~95% of INR 2,000 cr FY27 revenue; H1 revenue was INR 853 cr (+2.7% YoY), so H2 needs ~INR 1,050 cr, and Avinashi is still shrinking YoY.

rows.label: Sri Lanka fourth factory and new US/UK customers
rows.why: Fourth factory (~500 machines) needs customer approval by end-March; a new US customer is expected from February 2027 and a new UK customer is already shipping, but Sri Lanka FY27 is tracking INR 150-170 cr vs INR 190 cr plan.

rows.label: Retail parent debt to equity conversion
rows.why: Management plans to convert parent debt to equity this financial year; consolidated net debt is INR 364 cr and Retail debt is rising, with external capital (PE or SME listing) to follow later.

rows.label: SPUK EBITDA breakeven then positive
rows.why: SPUK revenue grew 111.8% YoY to INR 38.1 cr in Q2 with GBP 4.5 mn order book, and management guided EBITDA breakeven in Q3 and positive in Q4 FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on the demand recovery, SPUK and FY28 (10-15% growth, Sri Lanka INR 400 cr) but cautious on FY27 revenue, cut to ~95% of INR 2,000 cr, with Sri Lanka and Avinashi lagging; answers on Sri Lanka approvals and Retail funding were hedged and sometimes deferred to other executive
